correctness.rationale: Exact divisor equality and Fock order at most two, via Hadamard factorization, give F=C exp(Az²+Bz)g_N. On the critical square lattice, the Gaussian-normalized sigma function is lattice-periodic in modulus after the standard quasiperiod correction. Division by sinh(√πz) cancels the deleted line zeros and gives a two-sided envelope exp(−√π|Re z|) on remote nonzero cell-centre disks; each extra deleted point adds |z|^-2 to the squared Fock integrand. A sector with Re(Az²)>c|z|² excludes A≠0; vertical cell strings of both imaginary signs exclude Im B≠0. For real B=t, |t|<√π gives exponential integrability; endpoints t=±√π remove horizontal damping on one half-plane, leaving the 2D tail (1+|z|²)^(-N), integrable iff N≥2. For N=1 the lower bound summed over p≥P and |q|≤p diverges as ∑1/p; |t|>√π creates exponential divergence. This is an analytic all-N argument; no finite sample substituted. Critical auxiliary uniform cell estimates inspected in package but the source preprint was unavailable in full.
